answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each node to a Wesolowski VDF: a continuous chain of modular squarings in which every result is the next input, preventing an attacker from shortening one proof by distributing its dependent steps across GPUs. Simulating many Sybil clones requires separate chains and preserves a strict per-identity wall-clock cost. A vertex reaches the harbor only after this work; even lotus-named identities gain no exemption.
